34876-the-blackwood-group.creator: Sir George Douglas
34876-the-blackwood-group.description: A book by Sir George Douglas. y that the reputation of 'Christopher North,' the man, has survived that of his works? Third in the great dynasty of Scottish literary sovereigns, he ascended the throne upon the death of Scott, reigned gloriously and held high state in the Northern Capital--whence in earlier days he had waged direst war--and at his death passed on the sceptre to Carlyle, from whom in turn it descended to Stevenson.

arxiv-2006-05556.title: Review of results using heavy ion collisions at CMS
arxiv-2006-05556.description: A 2020 arXiv research paper by . UUltrarelativistic heavy ion collisions at the laboratory provide a unique chance to study quantum chromodynamics (QCD) under extreme temperature ( ≈ 150 {\approx}150\, ) and density ( ≈ 1 / fm 3 {\approx}1\,/\,\text{fm}^{3} ) conditions. Over the past decade, experimental results from LHC have shown further evidence for the formation of the quark-gluon plasma (QGP), a phase that is thought to permeate the early Universe and is formed in the high-density neutron-star cores.

arxiv-2211-16204.title: Generic Networks of Votings
arxiv-2211-16204.creator: Ewa Zawiślak-Sprysak
arxiv-2211-16204.description: Abstract In this paper, we analyse results of the 15 th 15^{\textrm{th}} International Henryk Wieniawski Violin Competition by comparing the properties of its results network to the properties of generic networks of votings . Suppose that a competition Comp is given. In this competition, k k contestants are rated by n n jurors.

arxiv-2306-08358.title: On semi-continuity and continuity of the smallest and largest minimizing point of real convex functions with applications in probability and statistics
arxiv-2306-08358.creator: Dietmar Ferger
arxiv-2306-08358.description: Abstract We prove that the smallest minimizer σ ⁡ ( f ) \sigma(f) of a real convex function f f is less than or equal to a real point x x if and only if the right derivative of f f at x x is non-negative.

arxiv-2401-00912.title: ScatterFormer: Efficient Voxel Transformer with Scattered Linear Attention
arxiv-2401-00912.creator: Chenhang He, Ruihuang Li, Guowen Zhang, Lei Zhang
arxiv-2401-00912.description: Abstract Window-based transformers excel in large-scale point cloud understanding by capturing context-aware representations with affordable attention computation in a more localized manner. However, the sparse nature of point clouds leads to a significant variance in the number of voxels per window.

arxiv-2407-02664.title: The path towards contact-based physical human-robot interaction
arxiv-2407-02664.creator: Mohammad Farajtabar, Marie Charbonneau
arxiv-2407-02664.description: Abstract With the advancements in human-robot interaction (HRI), robots are now capable of operating in close proximity and engaging in physical interactions with humans (pHRI). Likewise, contact-based pHRI is becoming increasingly common as robots are equipped with a range of sensors to perceive human motions.

arxiv-2503-01963.title: Projection-angle effects when “observing” a turbulent magnetized collapsing molecular cloud. I. Chemistry and line transfer
arxiv-2503-01963.creator: A. Tritsis, S. Basu, C. Federrath
arxiv-2503-01963.description: Abstract Context. Most of our knowledge regarding molecular clouds and the early stages of star formation stems from molecular spectral-line observations. However, the various chemical and radiative-transfer effects, in combination with projection effects, can lead to a distorted view of molecular clouds and complicate the interpretation of observations. Aims.

arxiv-2504-05410.title: Fast Controlled Generation from Language Models with Adaptive Weighted Rejection Sampling
arxiv-2504-05410.creator: Benjamin Lipkin * Benjamin LeBrun * Jacob Hoover Vigly João Loula David R. MacIver Li Du Jason Eisner Ryan Cotterell Vikash Mansinghka, Timothy J. O’DonnellAlexander K. Lew Tim Vieira MIT ETH Zürich McGill Canada CIFAR AI Chair Mila Johns Hopkins Yale CHI FRO
arxiv-2504-05410.description: Abstract The dominant approach to generating from language models subject to some constraint is locally constrained decoding (LCD), incrementally sampling tokens at each time step such that the constraint is never violated. Typically, this is achieved through token masking : looping over the vocabulary and excluding non-conforming tokens. There are two important problems with this approach.

arxiv-2506-02549.title: Navigating Phase Transitions with Path-Finding Algorithms: A Strategic Approach to Replica Exchange Monte Carlo
arxiv-2506-02549.creator: Akie Kowaguchi, Katsuhiro Endo, Kentaro Nomura, Shuichi Kurabayashi, Paul E. Brumby, Kenji Yasuoka
arxiv-2506-02549.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Akie Kowaguchi, Katsuhiro Endo, Kentaro Nomura, Shuichi Kurabayashi, Paul E. Brumby, Kenji Yasuoka. The replica exchange method is a powerful tool for overcoming slow relaxation in molecular simulations, but its efficiency depends strongly on the choice of the number and interval of replicas and their exchange probabilities. Here, we propose a new optimization scheme based on the Dijkstra algorithm that constructs an optimal exchange path by representing replicas and their exchange probabilities as a graph.

arxiv-2509-03758.title: Learning functions through Diffusion Maps
arxiv-2509-03758.creator: Alvaro Almeida Gomez
arxiv-2509-03758.description: Abstract We propose a data-driven method for approximating real-valued functions on smooth manifolds, building on the Diffusion Maps framework under the manifold hypothesis. Given pointwise evaluations of a function, the method constructs a smooth extension to the ambient space by exploiting diffusion geometry and its connection to the heat equation and the Laplace-Beltrami operator.

arxiv-2510-01596.title: Limitations of strong coupling in non-Markovian quantum thermometry
arxiv-2510-01596.creator: Qing-Shou Tan, Yang Liu, Xulin Liu, Hao Chen, Xing Xiao, Wei Wu
arxiv-2510-01596.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Qing-Shou Tan, Yang Liu, Xulin Liu, Hao Chen, Xing Xiao, Wei Wu. We investigate quantum thermometry using a single-qubit probe embedded in a non-Markovian environment, employing the numerically exact hierarchical equations of motion (HEOM) to overcome the limitations of Born–Markov approximations. Through a systematic analysis of the dynamical and steady-state behavior of the quantum signal-to-noise ratio (QSNR) for temperature estimation, we identify several key findings that challenge the conventional expectation that strong coupling necessarily enhances thermometric performance.

arxiv-2510-17942.title: Trust in foundation models and GenAI: A geographic perspective
arxiv-2510-17942.creator: Grant McKenzie, Krzysztof Janowicz, Carsten Keßler
arxiv-2510-17942.description: Abstract Large-scale pre-trained machine learning models have reshaped our understanding of artificial intelligence across numerous domains, including our own field of geography. As with any new technology, trust has taken on an important role in this discussion. In this chapter, we examine the multifaceted concept of trust in foundation models, particularly within a geographic context.

beaumont-knight-burning-pestle-1613.title: The Knight of the Burning Pestle
beaumont-knight-burning-pestle-1613.creator: Francis Beaumont
beaumont-knight-burning-pestle-1613.description: A grocer and his wife hijack a play to make their apprentice its chivalric hero.

plos-pone-0000294.creator: Lei Li, Xiangfeng Wang, Rajkumar Sasidharan et al.
plos-pone-0000294.description: PLOS ONE research article. Global Identification and Characterization of Transcriptionally Active Regions in the Rice Genome

pmc-10572793.title: Genetic Variant HLA-DRB1*0403 and Therapeutic Response to Disease-Modifying Therapies in Multiple Sclerosis: A Case-Control Study
pmc-10572793.creator: Esteban Alejandro Gomez-Gaitan, Yessica Eleanet Garcia-Ortega, Ana Miriam Saldaña-Cruz, Betsabe Contreras-Haro, Jorge Ivan Gamez-Nava, Emilio Edsaul Perez-Guerrero, Cesar Arturo Nava-Valdivia, Sergio Gallardo-Moya, Alejandra Martinez-Hernandez, Laura Gonzalez Lopez, Blanca Esthela Rios-Gonzalez, Jaz
pmc-10572793.description: Multiple sclerosis (MS) is a chronic and demyelinating disease with an autoimmune origin, which leads to neurodegeneration and progressive disability. Approximately 30 to 50% of patients do not respond optimally to disease-modifying therapies (DMTs), and therapeutic response may be influenced by genetic factors such as genetic variants.

pmc-10598627.title: Photosynthetic and transcriptome responses to fluctuating light in Arabidopsis thylakoid ion transport triple mutant
pmc-10598627.creator: Peter J. Gollan, Steffen Grebe, Lena Roling, Bernhard Grimm, Cornelia Spetea, Eva‐Mari Aro
pmc-10598627.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Fluctuating light intensity challenges fluent photosynthetic electron transport in plants, inducing photoprotection while diminishing carbon assimilation and growth, and also influencing photosynthetic signaling for regulation of gene expression. Here, we employed in vivo chlorophyll‐a fluorescence and P700 difference absorption measurements to demonstrate the enhancement of photoprotective energy dissipation of both photosystems in wild‐type Arabidopsis thaliana after 6 h exposure to fluctuating light as compared with constant light conditions.

pmc-10648362.title: Detection of traumatic stress in the presence of traumatic experiences: the role of resilience factors in foster care children five years or younger
pmc-10648362.creator: Kimberly I Tumlin, Amanda Crowley, Brian Turner, Elizabeth Riley, John Lyons
pmc-10648362.description: BackgroundChildren less than five years of age comprised approximately 30% in 2020 of foster care entries in the United States, and they are consistently the largest foster care entry group. Very young children can respond differently to the same adverse life events.

pmc-10653780.title: Perioperative discordance in mesothelioma cell type after pleurectomy/decortication—a possible detrimental effect of neoadjuvant chemotherapy due to epithelial to mesenchymal transition?
pmc-10653780.creator: Luigi Ventura, Michelle Lee, Ralitsa Baranowski, Joanne Hargrave, Michael Sheaff, David Waller
pmc-10653780.description: OBJECTIVESThe goal was to evaluate the accuracy of preoperative histological assessment and the factors affecting the accuracy and the subsequent effect on postoperative survival after surgical treatment for malignant pleural mesothelioma (MPM).METHODSWe analysed the perioperative course of patients who underwent surgery for MPM in a single institution over a 5-year period.

pmc-10689299.title: Predictors for delayed awakening in adult glioma patients receiving awake craniotomy under monitored anesthesia care
pmc-10689299.creator: Huan-Tang Lin, Chun-Ming Lin, Yah-Yuan Wu, Wei-Han Chang, Kuo-Chen Wei, Yi-Chun Chen, Pin-Yuan Chen, Fu-Chao Liu, Ko-Ting Chen
pmc-10689299.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). PurposeDelayed awakening after anesthetic discontinuation during awake craniotomy is associated with somnolence during functional brain mapping. However, predictors of delayed awakening in patients receiving monitored anesthesia care for awake craniotomy are unknown.MethodsThis retrospective cohort study analyzed 117 adult patients with supratentorial glioma in or near eloquent areas who received monitored anesthesia care for awake craniotomy between July 2020 and January 2023 at Linkou Chang Gung Memorial Hospital.

pmc-11503095.title: Common contributing factors of diagnostic error: A retrospective analysis of 109 serious adverse event reports from Dutch hospitals
pmc-11503095.creator: Jacky Hooftman, Aart Cornelis Dijkstra, Ilse Suurmeijer, Akke van der Bij, Ellen Paap, Laura Zwaan
pmc-11503095.description: IntroductionAlthough diagnostic errors have gained renewed focus within the patient safety domain, measuring them remains a challenge. They are often measured using methods that lack information on decision-making processes given by involved physicians (eg, record reviews). The current study analyses serious adverse event (SAE) reports from Dutch hospitals to identify common contributing factors of diagnostic errors in hospital medicine.

pmc-11625991.title: Oxygen matters: Unraveling the role of oxygen in the neuronal response to cisplatin
pmc-11625991.creator: Jose Crugeiras, Aina Calls, Estefanía Contreras, Montse Alemany, Xavier Navarro, Victor J Yuste, Oriol Casanovas, Esther Udina, Jordi Bruna
pmc-11625991.description: Background and AimsCell culture is a fundamental experimental tool for understanding cell physiology. However, translating these findings to in vivo settings has proven challenging. Replicating donor tissue conditions, including oxygen levels, is crucial for achieving meaningful results. Nevertheless, oxygen culture conditions are often overlooked, particularly in the context of chemotherapy‐induced neurotoxicity.

pmc-11725336.title: Novel Coenzyme Q2 (CoQ2) Mutation in a Pediatric Patient With Primary Steroid-Resistant Nephrotic Syndrome Due to Coenzyme Q10 (CoQ10) Deficiency
pmc-11725336.creator: Shahad Alwazzan, Osama Alnwaihi, Neetha John, Lova Satyanarayana Matsa, Hammad O Alshaya
pmc-11725336.description: Coenzyme Q2 (CoQ2) mutations are a group of autosomal recessive mitochondria-linked diseases that result in coenzyme Q10 (CoQ10) deficiency (CoQ10: a cofactor in mitochondrial energy production). Its deficiency leads to multiple systemic clinical presentations; however, isolated steroid-resistant nephrotic syndrome (SRNS) is considerably rare.

pmc-12634367.title: The relationships of character strengths with job stress, mental wellbeing and perceived stress among financial professionals
pmc-12634367.creator: Talgat Kutebayev, Robert L. Lloyd
pmc-12634367.description: IntroductionCharacter strengths have been related to job stress, mental wellbeing and perceived stress, however, little is known about these associations among financial professionals. The aim of this study was to investigate the relationships between character strengths, job stress, mental wellbeing and perceived stress in this occupational group.

pmc-12642797.title: AI Grading of Lateral Canthal Lines: Novel Models for Unseen Synthetic Image Generation and Data Augmentation
pmc-12642797.creator: Ting-Ting Yang, Ching-Wen Ma, Chiu-Hsien Lee, Shi-Xuan Qiu, Cheng-Che E Lan
pmc-12642797.description: PurposeLarge and balanced datasets are required to train artificial intelligence (AI) algorithms but are often difficult to acquire using clinical dermatologic photographs. We aimed to develop a new diffusion-based generative AI algorithm that generates patient photographs with modifiable details, thereby creating large and balanced datasets for neural network training.

pmc-13052171.title: A First Quantification of Plant Endemism in the Manica Highlands (Zimbabwe–Mozambique) and the Significance of Open Habitats
pmc-13052171.creator: Jonathan Timberlake, Vincent Ralph Clark
pmc-13052171.description: The Manica Highlands is a tropical transboundary mountain system shared by Zimbabwe and Mozambique, covering 7400 km2. Although extensively botanized for over 100 years, with many known endemic plant species, these have never been comprehensively enumerated or their patterns of distribution determined.

pmc-13053679.title: Beyond Lymphocytic Inflammation: Immune Architecture as a Determinant of Renal Outcomes
pmc-13053679.creator: Kanishka Harariya, Thakur Rohit Singh, Ankita Kalra, Swarupanjali Padhi, Fayaz Ahamed
pmc-13053679.description: e with unsupervised clustering, the authors move beyond descriptive histology to propose biologically distinct inflammatory subtypes with prognostic relevance. A central strength of this work lies in its cell-resolved tissue profiling, which reveals a neutrophil-rich immune phenotype that is not adequately captured by conventional Banff-based scoring.

pmc-13088727.title: M1 macrophage-derived migrasomes ameliorate temporomandibular joint osteoarthritis via autophagy
pmc-13088727.creator: Guoliang Sa, Zhongyang Zou, Haoyu Zhou, Guodong Sa, Jing Zhou, Hanlin Tu, Yingliang Shi, Yuyan He, Yi Guo, Zhan Liu, Xuewen Yang
pmc-13088727.description: The interaction between synovial cells and chondrocytes plays a pivotal role in the progression of osteoarthritis. However, the contribution of migrasomes, recently identified vesicular organelles mediating intercellular communication, remains inadequately explored in this context. Here, we first confirmed the presence of migrasomes in both synovial tissues and synovial fluid samples from patients with temporomandibular joint osteoarthritis (TMJ-OA).

pmc-13122232.title: Music recognition based on diffractive neural networks
pmc-13122232.creator: Xingcen Ge, Zirui Feng, Qian Ma
pmc-13122232.description: SummaryDiffractive neural networks offer high-speed and energy-efficient computation for artificial intelligence hardware, yet their application to time-series signal processing remains underexplored. Here, we propose an electromagnetic diffractive neural network framework for music style and sentiment classification. Time-series audio signals are converted into log-Mel spectrograms and processed using a multilayer metasurface-based DNN.

pmc-13248909.title: Gut microbial metabolism of Flutamide attenuates its therapeutic efficacy against prostate cancer
pmc-13248909.creator: Shujing Li, Haiying Ding, Jiaqi Wang, Lingjie Yuan, Ying Zhou, Weiben Xu, Hang Yin, Mengqian Ye, Yuning Sha, Fangyin Li, Yousheng Liu, Zhengqin Zhu, Lulu Song, Xiangyu Jin, Liefeng Ma, Zhajun Zhan, Libin Pan, Luo Fang
pmc-13248909.description: Endocrine drugs serve as the cornerstone of prostate cancer treatment. Flutamide, a representative first-generation antiandrogen, has been relegated to the treatment of recurrent prostate cancer due to novel drug development and therapeutic resistance. Our study shows the gut microbiota contributes to this resistance.

pmc-13377795.title: Re‐Evaluating Propofol Infusion Thresholds and Delirium Risk in Mechanically Ventilated Patients: Critical Appraisal of Pharmacological Plausibility and Residual Confounding
pmc-13377795.creator: Shuantong Lin, Jie Zhu
pmc-13377795.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). lished in CNS Neuroscience & Therapeutics [1]. The topic is clinically important, and the dataset is valuable. However, we have significant concerns regarding the authors' interpretation of their findings and the clinical implications they have drawn. First, the study identifies an average infusion rate of ≥ 20 μg/kg/h sustained over 18 h as an independent risk factor for delirium (OR = 1.84, p < 0.001). However, this threshold appears inconsistent with established clinical practice and dosing guidelines.

pmc-13426125.title: Human-Centered AI in Sleep Health Management: Scoping Review of Stakeholder Perspectives and Co-Design Practices
pmc-13426125.creator: Dacheng Dai, Fangfang Xie, Jiahe Cui, Siyu Wang, Junhao Cai, Fei Yao, Guimao Wang
pmc-13426125.description: BackgroundSleep disorders represent a significant public health burden associated with cardiovascular and neurocognitive morbidities. While AI technologies offer potential for personalized sleep medicine, clinical integration remains limited. This translational disparity is often attributed to a lack of human-centered design, specifically insufficient stakeholder engagement in the development and implementation of these technologies.

pmc-13439110.title: Consensus statements on the definition, diagnosis, and management of oligoprogressive disease: results of an expert survey of Kazakhstan Cancer Society
pmc-13439110.creator: Dilyara Kaidarova, Indira Omarova, Samat Kaldarbekov, Nazgul Omarbayeva, Maia Dzhugashvili, Elena Ulrikh, Dina Alisheva, Bakhadyr Bereketov, Ilya Tsimafeyeu, Timur Mitin, Ning Li, Nicola Normanno
pmc-13439110.description: Aim:Oligoprogressive disease (OPD) has emerged as a clinically relevant and common scenario in oncology, reflecting progression in a limited number of metastatic sites while systemic therapy continues to control the majority of disease. Despite its increasing recognition, the definition, diagnostic approach, and management of OPD remain poorly standardized.

pmc-13553140.title: Inoculation with old‐growth microbes improves restoration quality and reduces non‐native encroachment after seven years
pmc-13553140.creator: Tanya E Cheeke, Reb L Bryant, Gunner Davies, Liz Koziol, James D Bever
pmc-13553140.description: Understanding the mechanisms that promote native seedling establishment in disturbed ecosystems is key to improving the biodiversity and function of landscape restorations. Over seven growing seasons, we examined the effects of site preparation technique, soil microbial inoculations, and their interactions on native plant establishment in the restoration of an invaded grassland.

pmc-13658258.title: Unusual paraneoplastic thrombocytosis in small bowel neuroendocrine tumor responding to 177Lu-DOTATATE
pmc-13658258.creator: Eve Piekarski, Anne-Ségolène Cottereau, Romain Coriat, Lise Willems, Lucas Bouys, Florence Tenenbaum
pmc-13658258.description: Neuroendocrine tumors (NETs) are often associated with paraneoplastic features including carcinoid syndrome in up to 30% to 40% of cases. However, paraneoplastic thrombocytosis is a rare NET-associated condition. We report the case of a 59-year-old woman referred for significant and unexplained weight loss. Biological evaluation revealed thrombocytosis (900 × 109/L).
